label: L=3 sequences, first copy step after <DEL> (outputting orig token 1)
explanation: Fires only in length-3 sequences (12 of 3350 dev activations are in L=4, none in longer sequences). It fires on every L=3 sequence at t=4, the step right after <DEL>, where the input is the echoed first token and the model outputs original token 1. That step holds 93% of activation mass, with precision 1.0. A weaker tail fires at t=5 (recall_idx 2, the last output) on about 28% of L=3 sequences at low magnitude (about 0.1-0.4 of max). It does not fire in the original phase, on the delimiter, or in longer sequences. Magnitude at t=4 varies with token identity (top examples start with r/h/3/2/q) and is lower when the sequence contains digits (n_digits 0 holds 65% of mass). Not fully characterized.

issues: The core claims hold. On the dev split the unit is active only in the copy phase, at t=4 and t=5. All activation mass is on L=3 sequences except 12 L=4 steps, at recall_idx 1 (t=5). The predicate (L==3)&(recall_idx==1) scores test precision 1.0, recall 0.775, F1 0.873 and mass recall 0.932, matching the reported numbers.

The missed activations are the weak t=5 tail on L=3 sequences (about 22% of L=3 sequences active there, 6.6% of mass). I could not explain them: (L==3)&(recall_idx==2) has precision 0.28. Adding correct==0, in_count>1, n_digits==0 or a token set taken from the top examples gave F1 0.25 or lower. This is a weak, small remainder, not a systematic class the predicate gets wrong.
There are no false positives. Widening to the whole L=3 copy phase lowers F1 to 0.78, so the predicate is the right one.

Minor overstatement: 'sequences without digits hold 65% of the mass' is roughly the base rate. (26/30)^3 = 0.65 of L=3 sequences have no digits, and they hold about 61% of the mass on dev. This is not evidence of a digit effect.
Minor: the activations are small in absolute terms (max 0.075 above threshold), and how strongly the unit fires at t=4 depends on the first token, which remains uncharacterized.
